item: swap_window gives the library lock back when its cleanup hits a MemoryError, and an open that waits for the window re-checks every second
status: shipped (local, rides the WAL follow-on, on #1426's merged form)
summary: A MemoryError forced at every instruction of swap_window's cleanup that can allocate (an instruction sweep, harness in wal-disk-pool/swap-window-memoryerror-2026-10-17/) left the exclusive library lock held at 5 of 10 sites on main and on the build the instances run (d269ec397), and at 2 of 13 on #1426 plus one lost wake-up: every later connecting() then blocked in shared(), which had no timeout, until restart. The write gate was never at risk (0 of 34 forced failures, 14 on main and 20 on #1426, left it held). Fixed: (a) swap_window reads the thread identity BEFORE it asks for the window and release_if_held_here(me) compares it, so no call sits between 'the holder is ours' and 'the holder is cleared' (the get_ident() call was a site); (b) shared() waits in steps of _RECHECK_S = 1.0 s inside the same 'while True: if not wanted: break' loop (R161-R165 shape, pinned by the existing dis test in tests/test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py), named as the longest a lost wake-up may cost and NOT a timeout (an open still waits as long as the window is held); (c) tests/test_swap_window_allocation_failures.py is the harness as a test: red on #1426's shape at exactly the two predicted sites, green after, with three mutants of the module's own source that the sweep must catch (identity call, cleanup whose second statement is skipped, wait with no step), a structural pin of the release (no call before the holder is cleared) and a behaviour test that the step is not a timeout. Residual, named in swap_window's docstring and in the test: the CALL of release_if_held_here itself, which no code after it can protect. Sibling not changed: connecting()'s cleanup can leave a shared level raised on the same kind of failure (main 1 real site of 3, #1426 3 of 7), which makes later swaps refuse with LibraryBusy until restart, a named refusal and not a hang (REPORT.md addendum).
